newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes little changed in thin, Asian market.
newsitem.headline: Crudes little changed in thin, Asian market.

text.p: Crude oil prices were mostly unchanged in Asia on Tuesday in a thin market with little fresh news to stimulate trading in either direction, traders said.

At 0720 GMT, SIMEX Brent crude futures were untraded. Indications for the contract were seen at levels slightly lower than the IPE close on Monday. December Brent was indicated at $22.82/23.00, compared with the previous day's IPE settlement of $23.01.
December NYMEX light crude on the ACCESS after-hours system stood at $23.35/23.37.
Brent/Dubai spreads were notionally assessed at levels similar to the previous day in Tokyo.
The January Brent/Dubai spread was assessed at $1.95/$2.05, while February was assessed at $1.88/1.93.

In the wet market, at least one January Qatar Land was widely believed to have been sold by a major to a Japanese company at a premium of about 45 cents above the official selling price. There was also a report that a second January Qatar Land was sold at a premium of 43 cents. The premium for the deal, which would be the first traded for January cargoes of light crude, was several cents higher than December.

In regional crudes, traders said December cargoes of Minas have traded briskly. They said Australia has purchased about 800,000 barrels of the Indonesian crude, while China has also made some purchases. This meant that only about one million barrels of the crude for December loading are still available, traders said. Widuri and Cinta have also attracted buying interest they said.
An Asian crude trader noted that one factor that might inject the market with bearish sentiment is the possibility of West African crudes heading to the Far East.
